teacher_review_theme: Core Bernoulli variables versus Application SLO
teacher_scientific_note: Recognizing pressure, speed and elevation is a sound introductory Knowledge item (A); it is not by itself an Application-level use of Bernoulli’s equation, the demand of official summative B-40.

Pressure work is converted into changes in kinetic and gravitational potential energy, so source A is scientifically correct. Attribution to the exact original printed NBF derivation on pp.99–101 is not yet independently checked.
P+½ρv²+ρgh is the proper simplified along-streamline ideal-fluid equation with no external shaft work or significant losses; all three terms have pressure units, original C.
ρ is mass per unit volume, and its appearance in kinetic and height terms is consistent with the constant-density textbook model. Original C is correct.
½ρv² arises from (½mv²)/V and has units J/m³. Source B correct; it is not energy per unit mass.
ρgh = mgh/V is gravitational potential energy per unit volume for a specified height reference; source C correct.

Pressure is flow-work per unit volume under the idealized derivation because (PΔV)/ΔV=P; source D correct. Actual pressure energy is not a separately stored scalar independent of the chosen flow bookkeeping.
Each term P, ½ρv², ρgh has SI Pa = J/m³, so C is scientifically supported. Identification of the unit alone is Knowledge-level and does not certify official B-40 Application.
1 Pa =1 N/m², source B. This is dimensional Knowledge/prerequisite and not by itself summative B-40 Application; keep for student practice.
Height h is measured in metres, source A. This unit-recall item supports the model but is not evidence on its own of applying Bernoulli’s equation in horizontal/vertical flow.
When two comparison points share elevation and the ideal-model assumptions hold, ρgh cancels and P+½ρv² is constant along a streamline, original C.

The prepared derivation uses steady incompressible inviscid flow; Bernoulli also requires along-streamline interpretation in the general case and neglects appreciable external work/losses. Original A.

teacher_review_theme: Outlet pressure work negative for chosen control fluid
teacher_scientific_note: Source D is supported: external outlet pressure resists the rightward movement of the selected fluid segment, giving −P₂ΔV. Work sign depends on whether considering pressure forces acting on fluid or work fluid does on surroundings; original notation source not independently checked.
W=(PA)Δx=PΔV for an approximately uniform pressure acting through the element’s cross section; source B has correct units J.
ΔV=AΔx for a short segment with area A and displacement Δx, source C. This assumes the relevant normal cross-section and a simple slab/plug-flow construction.

teacher_review_theme: Equal displaced volumes are continuity prerequisite
teacher_scientific_note: Source A follows from steady incompressible leak-free unbranched continuity over the same Δt. This concept directly supports B-36 continuity and is used in Bernoulli derivation, but does not by itself explain/apply pressure–speed–height Bernoulli B-40.

teacher_review_theme: Two points on same ideal streamline
teacher_scientific_note: Source B identifies comparison points on a flowing streamline; in an irrotational flow the constant may also be common to different streamlines, but general steady inviscid Bernoulli constant can vary across streamlines.

teacher_review_theme: Volumetric flow rate as continuity prerequisite
teacher_scientific_note: Given uniform normal speed (or cross-sectional average), Q=V/Δt=Av, original A. This is a prerequisite continuity relation, not a standalone Bernoulli pressure/height application. The prepared source says uniform speed and does not imply all flow profiles are uniform.

teacher_review_theme: Historical physicist and textbook information box
teacher_scientific_note: Daniel Bernoulli is the name associated with Bernoulli’s equation, so source D is correct. The claim that the original printed NBF information box at pp.99–101 credits him specifically has not been directly verified; this Knowledge fact is not a B-40 Application item.
